title: Find a Research Gap: 7 Moves That Work
description: A practical seven-step workflow for finding and validating a defensible research gap with Google Scholar, Scopus, comparison tables, and careful AI assistance.

pages.heading: Find a Defensible Research Gap in 7 Moves
pages.text: Turn a broad field into one specific limitation you can test—without claiming that nobody has studied it.
pages.alt: Graduate researcher narrowing a large collection of engineering literature into one focused research question

pages.heading: 1. Search With Real Terms
pages.text: Combine the problem, application and constraint. In Scholar, use phrases, date filters, Cited by and Related articles to reach relevant work.
pages.alt: Research scholar refining search terms and filters to narrow recent academic literature

pages.heading: 2. Build a Comparison Matrix
pages.text: For each paper, record the problem, dataset, method, baselines, metrics, result, limitation and future work.
pages.alt: Graduate research team organizing papers into a structured literature comparison matrix

pages.heading: 3. Hunt for Repeated Limits
pages.text: Look for reused datasets, weak baselines, class imbalance, missing real-world tests, high compute cost or poor robustness.
pages.alt: Researcher identifying repeated datasets and missing validation patterns across engineering papers

pages.heading: 4. Test the Gap Twice
pages.text: Run a broad search, then a narrow synonym-rich search in Scholar and Scopus. If recent work solves it, refine the dataset, condition or constraint.
pages.alt: Graduate researcher cross-checking a possible research gap across two scholarly databases

pages.heading: 5. Make AI Show Its Work
pages.text: Use AI to compare your notes—not invent evidence. Verify every citation, dataset, claim and limitation in the original paper.
pages.alt: Researcher checking an AI-assisted literature synthesis against original journal papers

pages.heading: 6. Write the Gap Precisely
pages.text: Use this structure: what exists, what remains limited, why it matters, and what your study will investigate.
pages.alt: Engineering team planning a precise missing bridge segment as a metaphor for a research gap

pages.heading: 7. Turn It Into an Experiment
pages.text: Define the dataset, baseline, proposed change, evaluation metrics and real condition that will test whether the gap matters.
pages.alt: Graduate scholar converting a literature gap into a measurable engineering experiment

pages.heading: Run the Final Novelty Check
pages.text: Search again using your method, application, dataset and constraint. A defensible gap survives recent-paper review and leads to measurable objectives.
pages.alt: Graduate researcher completing a final evidence check before confirming a research topic
